investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Swarm cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both sets of nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~140–153 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agent Swarm scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which depends on a schedulable pod; scheduling failure prevents this call from completing successfully.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots are in use by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity; if the selector was broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be consuming the finite VM resource slots, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

Lower probability — cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and the absence of scale-out suggest autoscaling is either disabled or not provisioned for this node type.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so the check produced zero evidence and violated the remote-agent-state expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure originates at the infrastructure scheduling layer before any application code runs. The eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers pod creation; that pod never becomes schedulable, so the probe times out and returns no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 147s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153090, status=fail, endedAt=2026-06-24T20:14:36.989Z — eval exceeded the 147s unschedulable threshold before any agent was created.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the agent-creation or state-polling steps.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 140s — the upstream create check failed first, confirming the scheduling block precedes state polling.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s — the downstream runtime check also failed, confirming the capacity exhaustion affects the entire remote-agents VM pool.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905 (lines 1904-1905): runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with type 'remote'; if createAgent blocks on an unschedulable pod, no evidence is ever written.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none produced because agent creation never completed.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pod. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only two nodes are even candidates for remote-agent pods. If those two nodes are undersized or their VM resource limit is set too low, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying the VM resource, preventing new scheduling. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) but prior failed runs may not have completed cleanup.

Lower confidence — node affinity/selector values in the pod spec are too restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise serve remote agents. This would be a configuration issue rather than a capacity issue, but cannot be distinguished from capacity exhaustion without inspecting current node resource allocations.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Swarm cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both sets of nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~140–153 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agent Swarm scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which depends on a schedulable pod; scheduling failure prevents this call from completing successfully.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots are in use by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity; if the selector was broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be consuming the finite VM resource slots, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

Lower probability — cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and the absence of scale-out suggest autoscaling is either disabled or not provisioned for this node type.

Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so the check produced zero evidence and violated the remote-agent-state expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure originates at the infrastructure scheduling layer before any application code runs. The eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers pod creation; that pod never becomes schedulable, so the probe times out and returns no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only two nodes are even candidates for remote-agent pods. If those two nodes are undersized or their VM resource limit is set too low, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity. possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the VM slot quota is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the effective scheduling pool is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, the pool could have shrunk unexpectedly.

Tertiary — VM pool not scaled to handle concurrent eval probes: all three sibling checks ran in close succession (ending at ~20:12, ~20:14, ~20:17) and each required a kata peer-pod VM slot; if the pool is sized for steady-state traffic only, concurrent eval probes could exhaust it.

Lower confidence — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange change that reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable count on the 2 matching nodes; no source evidence supports this directly but it is consistent with the scheduler output.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe node output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (not exhausted) on the 2 affinity-matching nodes would disprove VM resource exhaustion as the cause.
A successful re-run of remote-agent-create immediately after this failure with no infrastructure changes would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod affinity/selector was recently changed to intentionally restrict scheduling to only 2 nodes (and those 2 nodes have always had insufficient VM slots) would shift the root cause to a configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of remote-agent-runtime captured in eval history (lastPassingAt non-null) close to the failure time would suggest a sudden capacity drop rather than a chronic misconfiguration; the supplied history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, so this baseline is currently unavailable.
If the 4 non-matching nodes were recently relabeled or had their affinity labels removed, that change would be the primary cause rather than VM slot exhaustion on the 2 remaining nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the affinity-matching nodes before attempting agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout inside the agent-create probe.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod selector, alerting if the matching pool drops below a configured minimum (e.g., below 2 nodes).

Add a VM slot availability eval that queries the Kubernetes API for current kata.peerpods.io/vm usage across the cluster and warns when utilization exceeds a threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.
Add eval history retention so that lastPassingAt and previousStatuses are populated; this would allow future investigations to distinguish a sudden regression from a chronic never-passing state.
